question.text: An electric field of $1000 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m}$ is applied to an electric dipole at angle of $45^{\circ}$. The value of electric dipole moment is $10^{-29} \mathrm{C} \cdot \mathrm{m} .$ What is the potential energy of the electric dipole?

solution.text:
Potential energy of a dipole is given by $\mathrm{U}=-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}$

$=-P E \cos \theta$

[Where $\theta=$ angle between dipole and perpendicular to the field $=-\left(10^{-29}\right)\left(10^{3}\right) \cos 45^{\circ}$

$=-0.707 \times 10^{-26} \mathrm{~J}=-7 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~J}$
